I think getting rid of the large XMatrix glyph sheets is probably a good start.  And look into compression for the other images?

Flash is 98% full: about 61 KB left for the next port
Filed by Claude, an agent working under Rod's direction.

## Problem

The firmware image on `main` (c7405fd) uses 3,083,233 of the 3,145,728 bytes
in the app partition (98.0%), about 61 KB free. The next port will probably
not fit until something makes room. Pipes (#101) added about 260 KB and
XJack (#100) about 57 KB.

## Where the flash goes

The largest symbols in `.pio/build/stopwatch/firmware.elf` (`nm -S
--size-sort`), with the After Dark image present:

| Symbol | Bytes | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pacman_png` | 522,248 | Pacman's sprite sheet, built from `vendor/` |
| `grab_image_blob` | 346,858 | The Windows 95 screenshot for "screen grab" hacks (DecayScreen) |
| `matrix1_png`, `matrix2_png` | 256,368 each | XMatrix's large glyph sheets |
| `teapot_triangles` | 227,520 | Pipes' teapot (`teapot2.h`, float triangles) |
| `matrix1b_png`, `matrix2b_png` | 61,888 each | XMatrix's small glyph sheets |
| `ad_colour_rgb` | 61,440 | Flying Toasters' colour art |
| `pacman_pool` | 31,488 | Pacman's 24 pre-made levels |

Those eight data blobs are about 1.8 MB, well over half the image.

## Options (not yet tried or measured)

- Store the big blobs compressed and unpack them when the hack starts
  (Pacman, XMatrix, the grab image). Costs RAM and start time while the
  hack runs; check each against free PSRAM.
- Drop data a hack never uses at our settings. XMatrix registers
  `*matrixFont: small`, so check whether the large sheets are ever drawn.
- Make the grab image smaller (fewer colours, or a smaller picture scaled
  up).
- Pipes' teapot appears on about 2% of pieces. A build-time copy of
  `teapot2.h` with the floats packed as 16-bit values would cut it to a
  quarter or so, at some cost in precision. Leaving the teapot out changes
  the hack.
- A larger app partition. Out of bounds under the current rules (keep
  `app3M_fat9M_16MB` and never touch `ffat`), so it needs Rod's decision.

## Also seen

Pipes' incremental-redraw state (`pi` in `hacks/pipes_gl.c`) is 16,544 bytes
of internal RAM (`.bss`), held whether or not Pipes is running, because of
its 4,096-entry list table. A heap allocation made when Pipes starts, or a
smaller table, would give that back.

# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.13"
# dependencies = ["pillow"]
# ///
"""Turn an image into the C header that Maze's logo is read from.

The device has no PNG decoder, so the image goes in as a raw RGB565 blob with
a 1-bit mask. The layout is documented in
firmware/src/x11shim/include/ximage-loader.h.

Run with: uv run tools/make_logo_blob.py logo-50.gif --name logo_50_png \\
    -o firmware/src/x11shim/include/images/gen/logo-50_png.h
"""

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

OPAQUE_ALPHA = 128


def rgb565(r: int, g: int, b: int) -> int:
    return (r & 0xF8) << 8 | (g & 0xFC) << 3 | b >> 3


def build_blob(width: int, height: int, rgba: bytes) -> bytes:
    if not (0 < width <= 0xFFFF and 0 < height <= 0xFFFF):
        raise ValueError(f"size {width}x{height} does not fit the blob header")
    if len(rgba) != width * height * 4:
        raise ValueError(f"expected {width * height * 4} RGBA bytes, got {len(rgba)}")

    pixels = bytearray()
    mask = bytearray()
    stride = (width + 7) // 8
    for y in range(height):
        row = bytearray(stride)
        for x in range(width):
            r, g, b, a = rgba[(y * width + x) * 4 :][:4]
            opaque = a >= OPAQUE_ALPHA
            pixels += (rgb565(r, g, b) if opaque else 0).to_bytes(2, "little")
            if opaque:
                row[x // 8] |= 0x80 >> (x % 8)
        mask += row
    header = b"565M" + width.to_bytes(2, "little") + height.to_bytes(2, "little")
    return bytes(header + pixels + mask)


def c_header(name: str, blob: bytes, source: str) -> str:
    guard = f"XSHIM_{name.upper()}_H"
    lines = []
    for i in range(0, len(blob), 12):
        lines.append("    " + ", ".join(f"0x{b:02x}" for b in blob[i : i + 12]) + ",")
    body = "\n".join(lines)
    return (
        f"/* Generated by tools/make_logo_blob.py from {source}; do not edit.\n"
        " * Despite the name (maze.c asks for a PNG), this is the raw blob\n"
        " * described in ximage-loader.h. */\n"
        f"#ifndef {guard}\n"
        f"#define {guard}\n"
        f"static const unsigned char {name}[] = {{\n"
        f"{body}\n"
        "};\n"
        "#endif\n"
    )


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    from PIL import Image

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=(__doc__ or "").split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("image")
    parser.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="C array name")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--size",
        type=int,
        help="shrink to fit this many pixels square, keeping the aspect ratio "
        "(never enlarges)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
/* Shim replacement for xscreensaver's utils/ximage-loader.h. Not derived from
 * xscreensaver code.
 *
 * Upstream decodes a PNG. The device has no decoder, so the "image data" here
 * is a raw blob made on the Mac by tools/make_logo_blob.py:
 *
 *   bytes 0-3          the characters "565M"
 *   bytes 4-5          width, unsigned 16-bit little-endian
 *   bytes 6-7          height, unsigned 16-bit little-endian
 *   next width*height  pixels, row by row, each RGB565 as 16-bit little-endian
 *   remainder          mask, row by row, each row padded to whole bytes,
 *                      most significant bit first; 1 = draw the pixel
 *
 * The blob size must match its width and height exactly. */
#ifndef XSHIM_XIMAGE_LOADER_H
#define XSHIM_XIMAGE_LOADER_H

#include "x11shim/xshim.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Returns a colour pixmap, and writes its size and a depth-1 mask pixmap
 * through the pointers. Returns None (and writes zeros and None) when the
 * blob is not valid or memory runs out. The caller frees both pixmaps. Any of
 * the three pointers may be NULL (xmatrix passes no mask, and none is made). */
Pixmap image_data_to_pixmap(Display *, Window, const unsigned char *data,
                            unsigned long size, int *width_ret,
                            int *height_ret, Pixmap *mask_ret);

/* The image as a 32-bit XImage of RGBA bytes (alpha 255 where the mask is set,
 * 0 where not), upside down, row 0 being the bottom, as upstream gives it for
 * glTexImage2D. NULL for a bad blob or no memory; free it with XDestroyImage. */
XImage *image_data_to_ximage(Display *, Visual *, const unsigned char *data,
                             unsigned long size);

/* Upstream reads an image file. The device has no filesystem for hacks and no
 * decoder, so this always returns NULL, and a hack that loads an optional
 * picture carries on without one. */
XImage *file_to_ximage(Display *, Visual *, const char *filename);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif

# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.13"
# dependencies = ["pillow"]
# ///
import sys
import zlib
import lzma
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image

sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/rod/build/stopwatch-screensaver/tools")
from make_logo_blob import build_blob  # noqa: E402

IMG = Path("/Users/rod/build/stopwatch-screensaver/vendor/xscreensaver-6.16/hacks/images")
GRAB = Path("/Users/rod/build/stopwatch-screensaver/firmware/assets/grab-image.png")


def rle16(words: list[int]) -> int:
    # count bytes of a run/literal packbits scheme over 16-bit words
    out = 0
    i = 0
    n = len(words)
    while i < n:
        j = i
        while j < n and words[j] == words[i] and j - i < 128:
            j += 1
        if j - i >= 2:
            out += 1 + 2
            i = j
        else:
            k = i
            while k < n and k - i < 128 and not (k + 1 < n and words[k] == words[k + 1]):
                k += 1
            k = max(k, i + 1)
            out += 1 + 2 * (k - i)
            i = k
    return out


def report(name: str, im: Image.Image) -> None:
    rgba = im.convert("RGBA")
    blob = build_blob(rgba.width, rgba.height, rgba.tobytes())
    px = blob[8 : 8 + rgba.width * rgba.height * 2]
    words = [int.from_bytes(px[i : i + 2], "little") for i in range(0, len(px), 2)]
    colours = len(set(words))
    bits = max(1, (colours - 1).bit_length())
    idx = {c: n for n, c in enumerate(sorted(set(words)))}
    indices = bytes(idx[w] for w in words)
    print(
        f"{name:10} {rgba.width}x{rgba.height} raw={len(blob):7} colours={colours:5} "
        f"zlib9={len(zlib.compress(blob, 9)):7} lzma={len(lzma.compress(blob)):7} "
        f"rle16={rle16(words) + (len(blob) - len(px)):7} "
        f"idx{bits}bpp={len(words) * bits // 8:7} idx+zlib={len(zlib.compress(indices, 9)):7}"
    )


for n in ("matrix1", "matrix1b", "matrix2", "matrix2b", "pacman"):
    report(n, Image.open(IMG / f"{n}.png"))
g = Image.open(GRAB).convert("RGB")
g.thumbnail((466, 466))
report("grab", g)
report("grab-q256", g.quantize(256).convert("RGB"))
report("grab-q64", g.quantize(64).convert("RGB"))

questions.question: Which decoder should unpack the deflated blobs?

options.label: ROM tinfl + host zlib (Recommended)
options.description: Device uses the ESP32-S3 ROM's tinfl (no flash cost, nothing vendored); the native/dump builds link the Mac's zlib. Host tests check the format; one device run proves the ROM path.

options.label: Vendor miniz tinfl
options.description: Copy miniz's tinfl.c (MIT) and use it on both host and device: one decoder tested everywhere, ~5-10 KB flash, a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES row.

options.label: Write our own inflate
options.description: A small puff-style decoder of our own (MIT). Most code to write and test; same on host and device.

questions.question: What should happen to XMatrix's glyph sheets?

options.label: Keep large, compress all (Recommended)
options.description: Look unchanged. Large pair ~66 KB and small pair ~26 KB once deflated.

options.label: Keep large, stub out small
options.description: Look unchanged; replace the never-drawn small sheets with a stub header to save another ~26 KB. Adds a trap if anyone selects -small.

options.label: Switch to small font
options.description: Override *matrixFont: small and stub the large sheets. 16 px glyphs, twice the columns; saves ~66 KB more.

def test_deflated_blob_keeps_the_header_and_zlib_compresses_the_rest():
    blob = mlb.build_blob(2, 2, RED + GREEN + CLEAR_BLUE + WHITE)
    packed = mlb.deflate_blob(blob)
    assert packed[:8] == b"565Z" + blob[4:8]
    assert zlib.decompress(packed[8:]) == blob[8:]


def test_deflate_option_writes_a_565z_blob_of_the_same_image(tmp_path):
    src = make_image(tmp_path, (64, 64))
    plain, packed = tmp_path / "plain.h", tmp_path / "packed.h"
    assert mlb.main([str(src), "--name", "n", "-o", str(plain)]) == 0
    assert mlb.main([str(src), "--name", "n", "--deflate", "-o", str(packed)]) == 0
    raw, z = blob_from_header(plain), blob_from_header(packed)
    assert z[:4] == b"565Z"
    assert z[4:8] == raw[4:8]
    assert zlib.decompress(z[8:]) == raw[8:]
    assert len(z) < len(raw)
